questions.q: 'There isn't ___ milk left' vs 'Would you like ___ tea?'
questions.a: any / some — negation takes 'any', polite offer takes 'some' even in a question. A wrong answer 'some' in the first shows the polarity rule missing.

questions.q: '___ money do you have?' much or many — and why?
questions.a: 'much' — money is uncountable. A wrong answer 'many' reveals the count/mass partition isn't built yet.

questions.q: Point correctly: '___ shoes here are mine, but ___ over there are yours.'
questions.a: 'these' (near + plural) and 'those' (far + plural). A wrong answer 'this/them' mixes the distance and number axes.

questions.q: Beyond a/an/the sits the ______ family: this/that/these/those (pointing), my/your/our (possession), some/any/many/much/few/little (quantity).
Fill in the blank: Beyond a/an/the sits the ______ family: this/that/these/those (pointing), my/your/our (possession), some/any/many/much/few/little (quantity).
Fill in the blank: Axis 1 — ______: this/these = near (singular/plural), that/those = far.
What is Beyond a/an/the sits the determiner family? State the definition given in this lesson.
questions.a: Beyond a/an/the sits the determiner family: this/that/these/those (pointing), my/your/our (possession), some/any/many/much/few/little (quantity).

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Axis ______ — pointing: this/these = near (singular/plural), that/those = far.
What common mix-up does this lesson flag about Beyond a/an/the sits the determiner family?
questions.a: Students use 'much' with countables ('much students'), 'some' in negatives ('I don't have some money'), and mix this/these by number.

questions.q: What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student selects the right determiner family member — demonstrative by distance/number, quantifier by countability and sentence polarity (some+ / any−?).
